title: MacInnes stars as GB top medals table at Europeans
description: Great Britain finish top of the medals table at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris as Keanna MacInnes helps them win two golds on Sunday.
fullText:
Great Britain finished top of the medals table at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris after Keanna MacInnes helped them win two golds on Sunday's final day of competition.

The 24-year-old sealed victory in the 200m butterfly with a new Scottish record of two minutes 5.90 seconds, then swam the fly leg as Great Britain won the women's 4×100m medley.

Angharad Evans followed up her gold in the individual 100m breaststroke with the fastest ever women's relay breaststoke leg as the team, which also included Lauren Cox and Freya Colbert, stormed to victory in a championship record three minutes 53.50 seconds.

The relay win secured top spot on the medal charts over Italy, whom they beat by a tenth of a second, with Great Britain finishing on 14 golds to second-placed Italy's 13.

The British squad also won four silvers and eight bronzes in the French capital, with 14 of their 26 medals coming in swimming events.

The swimmers secured eight golds, two silvers and four bronzes, including victory for 18-year-old Filip Nowacki in the men's 200m breaststroke on Thursday.

They also won two golds, two silvers and three bronzes in diving and four golds and a bronze in artistic swimming.

They topped the medal table in swimming and artistic swimming and were fourth in the diving table.

title: Liebmann and Douglass set world records on same day
description: Germany's Johannes Liebmann and American Kate Douglass set swimming world records on Saturday, dazzling crowds at events in Paris and California.
fullText:
Germany's Johannes Liebmann and American Kate Douglass set swimming world records on Saturday, dazzling at events held in Paris and California.

Liebmann, 19, knocked nearly four seconds off the men's 1500m freestyle record as he claimed his first international gold medal at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.

He completed the distance in 14 minutes 26.79 seconds - 3.88secs faster than the previous record which was set by American Bobby Finke at the 2024 Olympics, also held in the French capital.

Liebmann became the first swimmer to go under 14:30 for the distance as he slashed the most time off the record since Australia's Grant Hackett in 2001.

Three-time Olympic champion Hackett took more than seven seconds off when he swam 14:34.56 - a record which stood for 10 years.

Douglass broke the women's 50m freestyle record for the second time this summer, achieving her feat in California during heats at the Pan Pacific Championships.

The two-time Olympic champion, 24, clocked 23.49secs to regain the record from Gretchen Walsh.

Douglass swam 23.59 in June before compatriot Walsh lowered the mark to 23.55 nine days later.

title: PSG sign World Cup final match-winner Torres from Barcelona
description: Ferran Torres, who scored the winning goal for Spain at the World Cup, has joined European champions Paris St-Germain from Barcelona.
fullText:
Ferran Torres, who scored the winning goal for Spain at the World Cup, has joined European champions Paris St-Germain from Barcelona.

The 26-year-old has signed a deal with the French champions until 2031 for a reported fee of about 50m euros (£42.7m).

He scored the extra-time winner against Argentina to help Spain claim their second men's World Cup last month, while his stock had already risen considerably after a strong season with Barcelona.

The forward scored 21 goals in 49 appearances in all competitions, providing three assists, and helped Barcelona win the La Liga title.

PSG, managed by former Barcelona coach and player Luis Enrique, have won the Champions League in the past two seasons.

Torres is the second high-profile forward PSG have signed this summer after the arrival of Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco.

PSG added to their silverware collection on Wednesday by beating Aston Villa 2-1 to win the Uefa Super Cup.

Torres has been at Barcelona since 2022 having previously spent two years at Manchester City.

He has scored 25 goals in 65 appearances for Spain and made his debut for the national team under Enrique.

title: GB teenager Nowacki wins dramatic European gold
description: British teenager Filip Nowacki claims a dramatic gold in the men's 200m breaststroke final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.
fullText:
British teenager Filip Nowacki claimed a dramatic gold in the men's 200m breaststroke final at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.

The 18-year-old finished with a late burst in two minutes 7.70 seconds to edge out Dutch swimmer Caspar Corbeau (2:07.78).

Luka Mladenovic of Austria was third (2:08.91), while Briton Gregory Butler finished fifth in 2:09.45.

Nowacki made history for Jersey last month by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Meanwhile, Lauren Cox and Freya Colbert both won bronze medals for Great Britain.

Cox was third in the women's 50m backstroke final as 19-year-old Italian Sara Curtis won the race in a world record time of 26.56s.

Curtis broke Australian Kaylee McKeown's previous record by 0.23 seconds with a time of 26.63s in the semi- final on Wednesday and improved on that with her victory a day later.

Mary-Ambre Moluh of France was second with 27.06 and Cox was third in 27.15.

Colbert was third, with 1:55.81, in the women's 200m freestyle final as she finished behind winner Barbora Seemanova, who set a championship record of 1:54.38, with Marrit Steenbergen of the Netherlands second in 1:54.65.

Meanwhile, France's Florent Manaudou, who won the 50m freestyle gold at the 2012 Olympics, has said he will retire after his participation at the European Aquatics Championships.

The 35-year-old claimed bronze in the men's 50m freestyle at the 2024 Olympics in Paris and told France TV: "Two years later, I'm announcing the end."

Overall, Manaudou won six Olympic medals across four appearances at the Games, with three silvers and two bronzes in addition to his gold.

title: Liverpool believe Ibrahim Mbaye deal is ‘too expensive’
description: Liverpool consider a deal for Paris Saint-Germain forward Ibrahim Mbaye to be ‘too expensive’, according to transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano.Liverpool are pushing to sign Mbaye, with the club loo...
fullText:
Liverpool consider a deal for Paris Saint-Germain forward Ibrahim Mbaye to be 'too expensive', according to transfer reporter Fabrizio Romano.

Liverpool are pushing to sign Mbaye, with the club looking to sign a natural right winger to replace Mohamed Salah.

The Reds have already held talks with his representatives over a potential move, but could be priced out of a move for the Senegal international.

PSG reportedly want close to €200 million for Mbaye and Bradley Barcola combined, an amount the Reds consider too steep.

The 18-year-old is the UEFA Champions League holders' youngest-ever starter, but has found it difficult to nail a starting berth. He is expected to leave this summer to get more playing time.

Bayer Leverkusen, FC Porto and RB Leipzig have also been linked with Mbaye, but the youngster prefers to join Liverpool.

It remains to be seen whether PSG would reduce their valuation to allow the right-winger to join the Reds.

Liverpool appear to be prioritising a move for Barcola, which could hinder Mbaye's move to the Merseyside giants.

Liverpool plan to use the France international as their left winger, with Rio Ngumoha moving to the right flank.

Liverpool could struggle next season if they fail to sign a natural right winger. Federico Chiesa is their only senior option in the position, but the Italian has struggled with injuries since joining the club.

The Reds should try to reach a compromise with PSG for Mbaye or look elsewhere for a right-wing specialist.

title: Barcelona forward’s move to PSG set to be completed today or tomorrow
description: After Ronald Araujo, Ferran Torres is set to become the next Barcelona player to leave the club.The Spanish international is widely expected to join Paris Saint-Germain after a brilliant 2025/26 and W...
fullText:
After Ronald Araujo, Ferran Torres is set to become the next Barcelona player to leave the club.

The Spanish international is widely expected to join Paris Saint-Germain after a brilliant 2025/26 and World Cup campaign.

Ferran's move is currently of when and not if; with the player soon expected to travel to the French capital.

According to Cadena SER, the agreement between Barcelona and PSG for Ferran's transfer could be finalised between today and tomorrow.

Ferran Torres to soon become a PSG player. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images)

The forward already has an agreement in place with the French club and is ready to travel to Paris in the coming hours to undergo his medical.

Ferran did not train with Barcelona on Thursday, having also been excused the previous day.

Negotiations between the two clubs have entered their final phase, with PSG having long since agreed personal terms with the player.

All that remains is for the definitive transfer terms to be settled, with the operation set to be closed for a figure of around €55 million.

For Barcelona, recouping such a sum for a player with just one year left on his contract represents excellent business, even if losing a World Cup final hero is far from ideal.

Ferran's exit could pave the way for Rodri to join Barcelona. (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images)

Ferran's exit is closely tied to Barcelona's other major ongoing operation, the pursuit of Rodri.

The Catalans have already sent Manchester City a second proposal worth €60 million, made up of a fixed fee and variables, having seen an initial €50 million bid rejected.

However, reports suggest City have also turned down this latest offer.

Barcelona remain confident the deal will ultimately happen, with the club planning to make a third and definitive offer in the region of €70 million, comprising €60 million fixed plus €10 million in add-ons.

The funds generated by Ferran's departure will naturally aid Barcelona's efforts to get the Rodri deal over the line, both financially and in terms of squad registration.

With one exit nearing completion, the Catalans will hope it paves the way for a marquee arrival, as they look to reshape their squad before the window closes.

title: GB's Evans wins European gold in 100m breaststroke
description: Great Britain's Angharad Evans won her first European Championship gold in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.
fullText:
Great Britain's Angharad Evans won her first European Championship gold in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.

The 23-year-old comfortably finished first in a championship record time of one minute and 4.87 seconds, which was also a lifetime best and British record.

Having also broken the championship record in the semi-final, Evans claimed gold ahead of Ireland's Mona McSharry in second, while Italy's Benedetta Pilato took bronze.

Great Britain's Filip Nowacki, who made history for Jersey by claiming gold in the 200m breaststroke at the Commonwealth Games last month in Glasgow, was the fastest qualifier in the semi-final of the same event at the European Aquatics Championships.

The 18-year-old's time of 2:08.60 held off GB team-mate Greg Butler in the first semi-final, with the 25-year-old also progressing to the final.

GB's Amalie Smith picked up a silver medal in the 400m individual medley final, finishing 0.7secs behind Ireland's Ellen Walshe, with Poland's Justina Kozan claiming bronze.

The 16-year-old Smith, who won gold on Monday in the 4x200m freestyle relay, was also part of the part of the 4x100m freestyle relay team that finished fifth.

Another teenager, Italian Sara Curtis, also shone as she broke the women's 50m backstroke world record with a time of 26.63 seconds.

The 19-year-old bettered the world record set by Australia's Kaylee McKeown three years ago by 0.23secs in her semi-final.

title: Neto attracting Premier League interest
description: Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City. fullText:
Chelsea winger Pedro Neto has attracted interest from four Premier League clubs, with one believed to be Manchester City.

The 26-year-old Portugal international is not regarded as one of the 'untouchable' players at Stamford Bridge and could therefore move before the transfer deadline.

However, Chelsea insist they would demand a significant fee for the attacker, who joined from Wolves for £54m in 2024.

The club believe the market for wide forwards has been inflated by a lack of options for leading clubs, highlighted by the £117m fee paid for Morgan Rogers and Paris St-Germain's £145m valuation of Bradley Barcola.

Those figures have influenced Chelsea's valuation of Neto, who is known to be of interest to Manchester City where he would be reunited with former Blues boss Enzo Maresca.

Maresca and Neto are understood to have a strong relationship, and the winger is among those reported to have been frustrated by the Italian's departure midway through last season.

New manager Xabi Alonso has not commented on Neto's future, but he has played the winger in pre-season friendlies, including the 3-0 win over AC Milan on Saturday.

title: Can PSG do a three-peat and win six trophies this season?
description: Paris St-Germain aim to start their season as they hope to end it - by winning a European trophy.
fullText:
Paris St-Germain aim to start their season as they hope to end it - by winning a European trophy.

The back-to-back European champions could become only the second team to win three consecutive Champions Leagues this season.

But first the focus is on the Uefa Super Cup against Europa League winners Aston Villa in Salzburg on Wednesday (20:00 BST).

BBC Sport looks at how PSG are shaping up this season.

After years and years of failure and billions of pounds spent, Paris St-Germain finally won the Champions League in 2025.

And then they became one of only two teams to win consecutive Champions League trophies.

They hammered Inter Milan 5-0 in Munich in 2025 and then beat Arsenal on penalties in Budapest this year.

Only Real Madrid had won the Champions League back-to-back before - winning three in a row from 2016 to 2018.

It is something even the great teams like Pep Guardiola's Barcelona or Manchester City, or Alex Ferguson's Manchester United, or various Bayern Munich sides have not done.

Joining Real on three is the aim for Luis Enrique's side this season.

Going back to the start, only three other teams have managed to win three consecutive European Cups - Real Madrid, who won the first five from 1956 to 1960, and Ajax and Bayern Munich both in the 1970s.

In fact if you stretch it out to three European Cups in five years you would only have to add Liverpool (1977, 1978, 1981) to that list.

Paris St-Germain will play in six competitions this season (three of them being one-off finals) - and will be favourites to win each of them.

They are the Uefa Super Cup, Trophee des Champions (France's Community Shield), the Champions League, Ligue 1, the French Cup and the Fifa Intercontinental Cup.

Last season they won a joint record five, only failing in the French Cup where they lost to neighbours Paris FC in January. The season before they won four trophies.

No major team have ever won six pieces of silverware in a season before.

Away from PSG the record is Celtic's five in 1966-67 (including the Glasgow Cup), while several teams have won four - including Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich, Manchester United and Manchester City.

PSG may take some time to get into full flow this season, having had 16 players at the World Cup.

Six were involved until the final weekend - five for France and Fabian Ruiz for winners Spain.

Eight of their players scored at least one goal - which is a record for one club at a World Cup.

There are only 24 days between the World Cup final and the Uefa Super Cup - so some players will be far from rested.

It was not much better last season when they only had a month between the Club World Cup final, which came at the end of 2025-26 (losing to Chelsea), and the Super Cup.

In the Super Cup they came from 2-0 down to beat Tottenham on penalties after a 2-2 draw.

And they have been slow starters in the Champions League recently - needing a knockout phase play-off tie after failing to finish in the top eight both times - before finishing strongly to win.

PSG have had a consistent team over the past two seasons.

In fact they started the same 10 outfield players in both Champions League finals - with only the goalkeeper changing.

And those 10 players remain at the club.

Their summer signings so far have been Monaco midfielder Maghnes Akliouche, Aston Villa left-back Lucas Digne and 18-year-old Milan goalkeeper Alessandro Longoni.

The only departures so far have been Lee Kang-in to Atletico Madrid and Goncalo Ramos to AC Milan.

Bradley Barcola could join Liverpool in a deal worth about £100m.

All three were substitutes in the Champions League final.

PSG had tried to sign Leipzig and Ivory Coast forward Yan Diomande but had a bid of £102.5m rejected - and he went to Real Madrid instead for up to £120m.

Their focus now appears to be on Barcelona's Ferran Torres, who scored the only goal for Spain against Argentina in the World Cup final.

title: Ramsay-Peaty fifth in European Championships 100m final
description: Adam Ramsay-Peaty was beaten for the first time at a European Aquatics Championships as he finished fifth in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.
fullText:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty was beaten for the first time at a European Aquatics Championships as he finished fifth in the 100m breaststroke final in Paris.

The 31-year-old, who has 16 European Championships golds, had previously never lost a heat, semi-final or final at the event.

Olympic champion Nicolo Martinenghi won the race in 58.58 seconds, with Ivan Kozhakin finishing second and Italy's Simone Cerasuolo third.

title: Team GB claim relay golds at European Championships
description: Team GB secure three medals on the opening day of the European Aquatics Championships in Paris, while Jack Kelly sets a new Irish record to reach the breaststroke final.
fullText:
Team GB secured three medals on the opening day of the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.

The men's and women's 4x200m freestyle relay teams both collected gold, while Max Litchfield took bronze in the men's 400m individual medley.

James Guy, Duncan Scott, Matt Richards and Belfast's Jack McMillan came home first in the men's 4x200m relay final.

The quartet were first to touch home in a time of seven minutes 1.52 seconds, finishing ahead of France in second and Germany in third.

In the women's final, Freya Anderson, Leah Schlosshan, Abbie Wood and Freya Colbert powered into first place with a time of 7:45.93.

Hungary were second in 7:49.09, while Neutral Athletes B took bronze in 7:49.13.

Litchfield had to settle for third in the final of the men's 400m individual medley, finishing in 4:11.58.

Ilya Borodin claimed gold with a championship record of 4:08.17, while Italy's Alberto Razzetti was second in 4:10.40.

Jack Kelly twice broke the Irish 100m breaststroke record on Monday to reach Tuesday's final in Paris.

The New York native, who is Irish qualified through his mother, broke the record previously held by Darragh Greene in Monday's heats with a time of 59.27 but bettered that in the semi-final with a finishing time of 58.90.

Kelly finished second in the race behind Italy's 2024 Olympic champion Nicolo Martinenghi in 58.67.

"To go under 59 has always been a dream of mine and to actually see it on the board is just like 'wow," said 23-year-old Kelly.

"It's been an awesome start to the meet and I'm excited to see what I what I do next.

"It was exciting, the energy was there and to feed off it was what I did, it's been a really cool environment. I can hear the guys, they've been very supportive, we're very close and I couldn't wish for better teammates; the environment is great and something that is really cool to be part of.

The 100m breaststroke final will take place on Tuesday at 17:48 BST.

Meanwhile, a personal best was not enough for Belfast's Lottie Cullen to secure her place in the 200m backstroke final.

The National Centre Ulster swimmer, representing Ireland, finished sixth in her semi-final with a time of 2:12.22.

title: Tielemans cameo against PSG hints at Man Utd future
description: Manchester United's £35m signing Youri Tielemans makes an impressive debut in the 1-1 friendly draw against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.
fullText:
The sample size was only 26 minutes.

Yet the little combinations between Youri Tielemans and Bruno Fernandes after both were introduced in the second half of Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg drew an appreciative response from senior figures at the club.

With much made of United's activity - or lack of - in the transfer market this summer, it was good timing that Tielemans could make his debut when Mason Mount, arguably the club's player of pre-season, needed to be replaced after just 20 minutes.

Head coach Michael Carrick told Norwegian broadcaster VG post-match that Mount had come off as a precaution after taking a hefty blow to his foot. The former Chelsea midfielder walked freely past reporters to the team bus an hour after the final whistle.

Nevertheless, Tielemans was a surprise signing when Manchester United triggered a previously unknown £35m clause in the Belgian's contract at Aston Villa to agree a five-year deal.

There was a lot of debate in the immediate aftermath about how much football the 29-year-old, who made his professional debut for Anderlecht when he was just 16, had played.

Against PSG he did not do anything particularly special.

There were a couple of 45-yard cross-field passes that found their intended targets. There were some simple first-time lay-offs to team-mates within 10 yards.

There was also a short sprint just outside the United area to close down dangerman Khvicha Kvaratskhelia when Tielemans recognised the PSG star could be about to take possession within shooting distance.

He got there, won the ball and played a simple pass, taking the ball out of harm's way.

'Tidy debut' for Tielemans - how Man Utd rated against PSG

This isn't really what got the United contingent purring.

They were reacting to the little passes between Tielemans and Fernandes, which allowed United to ease their way out of trouble or move up the pitch.

Fernandes was the key man last season as United finished third. Nine goals and 21 assists was a decisive contribution in returning the club to the Champions League after a two-year absence.

Tielemans showed in his brief cameo he can take some of the pressure off the Portuguese.

"Youri has consistently been one of the most outstanding midfielders in the Premier League throughout the past seven years," said director of football Jason Wilcox on Tielemans' signing.

"He will add further composure, creativity and leadership to our squad.

"He has all of the technical qualities, as well as the ambition and mentality, to thrive at Manchester United."

If Wilcox reflects on those words as United head off to the Republic of Ireland for their week-long training camp in Maynooth, he can be quite pleased with himself.

It was only 26 minutes, but on that evidence, he has got it spot on.

Carrick has confirmed Marcus Rashford will rejoin the Manchester United squad for their trip to the Republic of Ireland.

Rashford, England team-mate Kobbie Mainoo and Argentina defender Lisandro Martinez are the final three players to return for United after the World Cup.

Although it was not expected Rashford would return to the club when he joined Barcelona on loan in July 2025, the La Liga champions failed to trigger a £26m option to buy the 28-year-old at the end of the season.

Despite interest elsewhere, there has been no deal, meaning Rashford will return to United for the first time since January 2025, when he moved to Aston Villa after falling out with former manager Ruben Amorim.

United are training at the plush Carton House hotel in Maynooth and have a friendly with Leeds United at Croke Park on 12 August.

They complete their pre-season programme against Amorim's new club AC Milan in Wroclaw on 15 August, when Rashford could make his first United appearance since December 2024 if Carrick decides Wednesday is too soon.

A former team-mate, coach and manager of Rashford, it has been felt if anyone can patch up the relationship between club and player - which includes his number 10 shirt being given to Matheus Cunha who is also due to be on the trip after a minor injury ruled him out of the Gothenburg encounter - it is Carrick.

"I've played with him. I played in the game he made his debut, so we have a history," Carrick said.

"We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together. Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie [Mainoo] and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them."

title: What strengths might Barcola bring to Anfield?
description: At first glance, Bradley Barcola looks like the natural successor to Luis Diaz, with the underlying data suggesting the Paris St-Germain forward could fill that void. fullText:
At first glance, Bradley Barcola looks like the natural successor to Luis Diaz, with the underlying data suggesting the Paris St-Germain forward could fill that void.

Opta's player similarity model rates the Frenchman as the winger whose output most closely resembled Diaz's across Europe's top five leagues in 2025-26 (78%), with Mohamed Salah (65%), Lamine Yamal (61%) and Vinicius Junior (61%) the next closest matches.

A closer look, however, suggests Liverpool would not simply be replacing one winger with another.

Barcola is a left winger by trade, having played almost all of his Champions League minutes for PSG on that flank, but his game is shaped by a centre-forward's instincts. He played as a striker until the age of 17, something reflected in his movement and shot selection.

Last season, he averaged 3.5 shots per 90 minutes in Ligue 1, placing him among the division's most active shooters despite operating from wide areas.

His 9.83 expected goals (xG) ranked in the 95th percentile among wingers across Europe's top five leagues, meaning only around 5% of wide players consistently found themselves in better goalscoring positions.

Barcola converted those chances into 11 league goals, outperforming his xG, while no PSG player or Ligue 1 winger recorded a higher xG total during the 2025-26 campaign.

Those instincts are reflected in how he attacks defenders. Barcola was the only player across Europe's top five leagues to average more than two shot-ending carries per 90 minutes (2.06), illustrating his ability to drive at opponents before creating shooting opportunities for himself.

He also averaged 8.69 touches in the opposition penalty area per 90 minutes - the seventh-highest figure among more than 1,500 eligible players - reinforcing the profile of a winger who consistently occupies goalscoring positions.

His shot map highlights a player who attacks dangerous central areas rather than settling for speculative efforts from distance.

The comparison with Salah is equally revealing. While both pose a significant goal threat, Barcola is a more direct ball carrier.

He attempted more take-ons per 90 than the Egypt forward last season (4.26 to 3.38), but created fewer chances (2.16 to 2.33), attempted far fewer crosses (1.15 to 4.89) and through balls (0.25 to 0.59).

The numbers point towards a player who looks to eliminate defenders himself rather than orchestrate attacks from wide areas.

There are also signs that his game continues to evolve under Luis Enrique.

Barcola's passing profile across his three Champions League campaigns at PSG has become increasingly focused on progressing play in the final third, reflecting greater tactical maturity. Rather than dribbling at every opportunity, he now shows a better understanding of when to accelerate attacks and when to recycle possession.

His work without the ball is another reason Liverpool's recruitment team are understood to admire him. Barcola ranked ninth across Europe's top five leagues for possessions won in the final third last season, a metric that reflects the aggressive pressing and intensity likely to be demanded under Andoni Iraola.

title: Barcelona await PSG offer for 26-year-old forward as doubts over future grow

fullText:
According to SPORT, FC Barcelona are preparing for what could be a decisive week in Ferran Torres' future, with growing expectations inside the club that Paris Saint-Germain will submit an official offer for the Spanish forward.

Although Ferran has not directly informed the club of any desire to leave, conversations with people close to the player have led Barça to believe that a move from PSG could arrive in the coming days, possibly even before the winger returns for pre-season on August 12.

The La Liga champions have no intention of forcing Ferran out, but they are equally clear that he will only be sold if a significant offer arrives.

So far, no formal negotiations have begun between the two clubs, but Barcelona are prepared for that to change quickly.

If PSG want to sign the 26-year-old, they will need to meet the club's financial expectations.

Barcelona were surprised by Ferran's recent public remarks, particularly his statement that the club must "show they want me."

PSG want Ferran. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

Within the club, those comments have been interpreted as a sign that the player may already be leaning towards a departure.

Barcelona had already informed Ferran that discussions over a new contract would not begin until September because of salary cap restrictions, following the same approach taken with other players such as Eric Garcia.

The expectation was that both sporting director Deco and head coach Hansi Flick would sit down with the player after his return from holiday to discuss his future.

However, there is now a feeling that PSG want to accelerate the process before those conversations take place.

Despite Ferran entering the final year of his contract, Barcelona are not willing to lower their demands.

The Catalans believe the striker market is extremely limited, while Ferran's value has risen following his performances at the World Cup.

If PSG fail to meet their asking price, the Blaugrana are prepared to keep the player for the entire season, even if that creates the risk of losing him on a free transfer in 2027.

Barcelona believe Ferran's representatives have been in discussions with PSG for some time and that personal terms may not be an obstacle if the French champions decide to move forward.

Likely to leave. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

Should the player ultimately decide against leaving, the Catalans remain willing to offer him a contract extension later this year, although the proposal would include no major salary increase.

While the club value Ferran's contribution, neither the sporting department nor Hansi Flick currently view him as an untouchable player within the project.

If Ferran eventually departs, Barcelona are expected to reinvest in a new centre-forward.

Julian Alvarez remains the club's primary target, and Barcelona intend to pursue him until the end of the transfer window.

Should that move prove impossible, the club have already identified two alternative striker profiles capable of strengthening the attack.

Liverpool, who finished fifth in the Premier League last season, 25 points behind champions Arsenal, could eventually end up paying Bayer Leverkusen £116m for Wirtz, while they shelled out a club record £125m to sign Isak from Newcastle in September.

And they could be about to break the bank yet again to bring in 23-year-old Barcola, who was part of France's squad at the World Cup.

He is right footed, although he prefers to play on the left wing, but can also play on the right or through the middle.

However, with PSG also having Georgia's Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and France's Desire Doue as wide options, Barcola does not play 90 minutes every match so a move to Anfield would give him more playing time.

With Mohamed Salah leaving on a free transfer at the end of last season having scored 257 goals in a hugely successful nine-year spell with the Reds, Liverpool clearly need to strengthen their attack.

France forward Hugo Ekitike ruptured his Achilles tendon in April and is not expected to play again in 2026, while Cody Gakpo, another who can play on the left and in the middle, has been linked with a move to Tottenham, although Liverpool say they do not want to sell.

The Reds' other current attacking options include 17-year-old Rio Ngumoha, Italy forward Federico Chiesa and new signing Victor Munoz.

Barcola has played 28 times for France and scored three goals in this summer's World Cup, including in the 6-4 loss to England in the third-place play-off.

However, like at club level, his game time was limited because of the skills of his 21-year-old PSG team-mate Doue.

Boss Didier Deschamps stuck with Ballon d'Or holder Ousmane Dembele on the right and rotated Barcola and Doue, with both men starting four of France's eight World Cup matches, but never in the same game.

At first glance, Barcola looks like the natural successor to Luis Diaz.

Liverpool chose not to sign a direct replacement after the Colombian's departure last summer, but the underlying data suggests the PSG forward could fill that void.

He also averaged 8.69 touches in the opposition penalty area per 90 minutes - the seventh-highest figure among more than 1,500 eligible players - reinforcing the profile of a winger who consistently occupies goalscoring positions.

His shot map highlights a player who attacks dangerous central areas rather than settling for speculative efforts from distance. Only Ousmane Dembele had a better combined shot volume with chance creation in Ligue 1, underlining Barcola's rare ability to both finish attacks and create opportunities for team-mates.

The comparison with Salah is equally revealing. While both pose a significant goal threat, Barcola is a more direct ball carrier.

He attempted more take-ons per 90 than the Egypt forward last season (4.26 to 3.38), but created fewer chances (2.16 to 2.33), attempted far fewer crosses (1.15 to 4.89) and through balls (0.25 to 0.59).

Barcola ranked ninth across Europe's top five leagues for possessions won in the final third last season, a metric that reflects the aggressive pressing and intensity likely to be demanded under Andoni Iraola.

That profile may suit Liverpool's evolving attack. With Wirtz excelling at releasing runners between the lines, and Ekitike and Isak expected to occupy central defenders, Liverpool arguably need another player capable of attacking space rather than demanding the ball to feet.

Barcola's willingness to make penetrative runs and arrive in goalscoring positions could provide exactly that.

Perhaps most encouragingly for any prospective buyer, there is reason to believe Barcola has not yet reached his ceiling.

A late physical developer, he has already transformed from a promising Lyon academy graduate into a two-time Champions League winner with PSG.

At just 23, his blend of pace, intelligent movement, elite shot volume, relentless pressing and growing creative output suggests one of Europe's most complete young wide forwards is still improving.

title: GB win two more golds at European Aquatics Championships
description: Great Britain win golds in the women's synchronised 10m diving and artistic swimming mixed duet at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.
fullText:
Great Britain won golds in the women's synchronised 10m diving and artistic swimming mixed duet at the European Aquatics Championships in Paris.

Maisie Bond and Lois Toulson achieved a score of 300.06 to clinch the women's 10m - just ahead of second-placed Germany (298.20) and Ukraine (286.20) in third.

"We came into these championships wanting to win and knowing it was possible," said Toulson. "We'd been training really hard and looking good I think.

"That was a [personal best] for us. To be able to do that and get a gold medal - we're really proud."

In the mixed duet, Isabelle Thorpe and Ranjuo Tomblin narrowly claimed their first European title in the event.

The pair won with a score of 258.2383 as they beat Spain by just 0.2650 to take victory, with Italy (255.1641) in third.

"It's incredible. I'm really happy and to have done it with Ranjuo is incredible." said Olympic silver medallist Thorpe.

"We didn't have the most smooth sailing preparation due to injury, but it's good we have been able to come through it and be on top."

Tomblin, who defended his title in the men's solo technical event on Friday, added: "Today is more special because I get to do it with Izzy, so it's incredible."

When Barcola returns from pre-season, he could request that PSG allow him to leave this summer. The attacker is expected to hope that the French champions will reconsider their position and agree to negotiate a potential transfer.

If PSG decide that a sale is possible, Bayern Munich are prepared to compete strongly for his signature and challenge Arsenal and Liverpool for the forward.

The German club’s interest adds further competition to an already difficult pursuit for the Premier League sides. Arsenal and Liverpool will now have to continue monitoring the situation while waiting to see whether PSG change their stance on Barcola’s future.

title: Liverpool dealt knockout blow in pursuit of talented forward

fullText:
Liverpool’s search for attacking reinforcements has largely centred on Paris Saint-Germain forward Bradley Barcola in recent weeks, but another name has consistently surfaced in discussions, AFC Bournemouth winger Rayan.

During the latest edition of Media Matters on Anfield Index, Dave Davis and David Lynch explored whether Liverpool’s long standing admiration for the Brazilian could realistically develop into a move this summer. Their conclusion was clear. Bournemouth’s circumstances, particularly following Junior Kroupi’s serious injury, make any deal appear increasingly unlikely.

The discussion began after Dave Davis highlighted fresh reports surrounding Bournemouth’s squad.

Referencing David Ornstein’s update, Davis noted that Junior Kroupi had suffered a foot injury in training that would require surgery and leave the forward sidelined for three to four months.

“I mean, that probably ends anything you think of Rayan coming in the short term,” Davis suggested. “It’s just hard to see now Kroupi’s got that injury.”

Lynch agreed that Bournemouth’s situation had become significantly more complicated.

“I think so. I just think the fee would be too much as well, obviously, as the release clause doesn’t kick in until next summer.”

That assessment points towards two major obstacles, Bournemouth’s strengthened negotiating position and Liverpool’s reluctance to pay well above the future release clause.

Rather than viewing this summer as the ideal opportunity, Lynch suggested Liverpool may actually benefit from delaying any move.

“The kind of money they’d be asking, I still think Liverpool would probably want a little bit more evidence of what he can do in the Premier League as well.”

He explained why next summer could present a much cleaner opportunity.

“The fact that the release clause comes in in 2027, I think it kind of works for everyone really, Liverpool get a bit of a closer look and an idea of just how good he is at that point. And then that release clause is sat there.”

Rather than rushing into an expensive transfer, Liverpool would gain another full Premier League season to evaluate the Bournemouth attacker.

Although Rayan has regularly been linked with Liverpool, Lynch admitted he had never believed a move was particularly realistic during this window.

“For me, I’ve never really bought into that, that was one that was possible, to be honest.”

He also pointed towards Liverpool’s own emerging talent as another factor that could influence future recruitment.

“In 2027, you also get a clearer idea of where Abe was up to, where Ngumoha is in his development as well.”

With several academy prospects continuing to impress under Andoni Iraola, Liverpool may have greater clarity before committing significant funds to another young winger.

Throughout the podcast, Bradley Barcola remained the dominant transfer topic, with Lynch repeatedly expressing confidence that Liverpool’s negotiations with Paris Saint-Germain are moving in the right direction.

Against that backdrop, Rayan appears to have slipped further down Liverpool’s list of immediate priorities.

Lynch concluded that Bournemouth’s latest injury setback only strengthens their determination to retain one of their brightest attacking talents.

“I think with Bournemouth having an injury there to Kroupi, they’re going to be even more kind of resolved to not let any big stars go.”

For Liverpool, patience may ultimately prove the smarter strategy. Rayan remains a player they admire, but the combination of Bournemouth’s asking price, the delayed release clause and Kroupi’s lengthy absence means this increasingly looks like a transfer for another window rather than this summer.

title: 'Only job I wanted': France turn to Zidane as coach
description: Zinedine Zidane was appointed France coach on Tuesday, as widely expected, following the departure of Didier Deschamps, the French Football Federation (FFF) announced."The France job was the only one I wanted," Zidane said at his unveiling in Paris, where he signed autographs and took photos with fans waiting outside the FFF headquarters after his appointment.
fullText:
Zinedine Zidane was appointed France coach on Tuesday, as widely expected, following the departure of Didier Deschamps, the French Football Federation (FFF) announced.

Zidane, 54, had long been viewed as the leading candidate for the role and had been waiting for an opportunity to take charge of the national team for several years.

He will replace Deschamps, whose tenure began in 2012 and ended earlier this month after France finished fourth at the World Cup.

Deschamps guided France to 2018 World Cup glory and the final four years later.

"For me, it's an immense joy... being able to become the coach of this French team. I don't have any other words," said Zidane, who takes over on a four-year deal that runs until the 2030 World Cup co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco.

"I'm holding myself back because I have so many emotions inside me. I'm ready for the challenge, that's what drives me today."

Former Real Madrid star Zidane, who was Deschamps' teammate in the 1998 World Cup triumph, has been readying himself for the role since leaving Real Madrid in 2021.

"The France job was the only one I wanted," Zidane said at his unveiling in Paris, where he signed autographs and took photos with fans waiting outside the FFF headquarters after his appointment.

"I've had offers over these four or five years to take charge of a club and I turned them all down for the French national team."

The former France playmaker, who scored twice in the 1998 World Cup final victory over Brazil and also won the 2000 European Championship as a player, has coached only one club, Real Madrid.

During his time with the Spanish giants, he led them to three consecutive Champions League titles in 2016, 2017 and 2018, an unprecedented achievement in the competition's modern era.

"I think it's a completely different job, that's for sure," said Zidane. "I've experienced the club side of it. Now this is something new for me, but it doesn't scare me."

Zidane will follow in the footsteps of former international team-mates Laurent Blanc, who coached the national side from 2010 to 2012, and Deschamps.

"I'm going to give everything so that this team keeps on winning. That's it, the only thing that drives me is being able to work for this France team and making sure it keeps on winning."

"'DD' (Deschamps) is 'DD', Blanc was Blanc and 'Zizou' is Zizou'.

"I will do things the way I know how to do them."

FFF president Philippe Diallo said he first met with Zidane in February 2025, shortly after Deschamps revealed he would step down from his role after the 2026 World Cup.

"There was one thing that struck me, that perhaps ultimately made the difference," said Diallo. "During the conversations we had, he said to me, 'President, I know how to win.'

"When he said that, I saw someone who had both the desire and the self-belief needed to lead France. That is what it takes for our national team to remain successful in the years ahead."

Zidane's first game at the helm of France will come away to Turkey in the UEFA Nations League on September 25. His first match at home will be against Italy at the Stade de France on October 2.

France captain Kylian Mbappe and all-time leading scorer welcomed the arrival of Zidane, posting a message that read "Welcome home" on Instagram.

Mbappe became the first player to win the World Cup Golden Boot twice after scoring 10 goals at this summer's tournament.

title: Europe's huge wildfires strain waterbomber capacity, aerial firefighting firm Avincis says
description: (Refiles story to remove erroneous spelling of company name in paragraph 5)  PARIS, July 27 (Reuters) - Europe's largest aerial emergency services firm Avincis is warning Europe is not ready for longe...
fullText:
(Refiles story to remove erroneous spelling of company name in paragraph 5)

PARIS, July 27 (Reuters) - Europe's largest aerial emergency services firm Avincis is warning Europe is not ready for longer and more extreme wildfire ‌seasons, with the company's chief executive telling Reuters that its firefighting aircraft are now needed almost year-round.

CEO John ‌Boag said longer European wildfire seasons and bureaucratic obstacles have exacerbated regional shortages of both aircraft and the experienced pilots needed to fly them.

"Globally, fire seasons ​are getting longer, aircraft are not moving between areas and pilots are becoming harder and harder to get," Boag said in an interview.

The comments by Boag, a helicopter pilot who began his career herding cattle in Australia's outback in a Bell 47 chopper in 1985, come as France and Spain battle historic wildfires after weeks of drought turned forests into major fire risks.

Lisbon-based Avincis says Europe is ‌under strain in part because the extra months ⁠of firefighting narrow the window for moving capacity between hemispheres, leaving gaps in capacity.

"Originally the peak period of the year over the summer was three or four months ... Now we have aircraft starting ⁠in March and April and going through to October," Boag said.

Wet winters only make the problem worse by increasing the growth of vegetal matter that can later turn into tinder. Just as concerning is the spread of fire risk further North.

"You're at a point where governments ​are going ​to have to be able to afford to have the aircraft ​available to cover a 12-month period, because commercial companies ‌can't go to the South (southern hemisphere) and earn more revenue over the off-season," Boag said.

Avincis has a fleet of 180 helicopters and 40 fixed-wing planes worldwide, including 22 Canadair waterbombers.

In Spain and Portugal, where it uses 47 aircraft, Avincis has flown more than 5,000 hours in firefighting operations so far this year, more than double the same period in 2025.

Europe has already made a collective purchase of 22 of the rugged water-scooping Canadairs from Toronto-based De Havilland Canada. After a decade-long production halt, ‌a new model is coming but won't reach its first customer, Greece, ​until 2028.

The Airbus A400M military plane has joined firefighting in France, ​dropping 20 tonnes of retardant. Others including China's Comac ​touted potential plane variants at last week's Farnborough Airshow and a French startup, HYNAERO, is in the ‌early design phase of an amphibious plane to be ​ready in 2032.

Firefighting is demanding, ​relying on low-level, precision flying in the face of unpredictable air currents. Experts say there is a shortage of experienced pilots and technicians.

Boag faulted European rules that require pilots to re-sit civil aviation exams if coming from abroad or ​the military.

"We need a pathway to be ‌able to get people into Europe quickly without the bureaucracy," Boag said. "The aerodynamics on a helicopter are the same ​in the military and the civilian world."

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency had no immediate comment on ​its pilot licensing rules.

title: Cycling in rude health thanks to awesome Pogacar and stringent testing
description: Tour de France fans were spoilt for choice in Paris when it came to drinking in the drama of cycling's greatest race.
fullText:
Tour de France fans were spoilt for choice in Paris when it came to drinking in the drama of cycling's greatest race.

Should their attention be all on Tadej's Pogacar's crowning as the joint most successful rider of all time, with five Tour titles?

But then what about Mathieu van der Poel's superhero-style victory on the final stage, climaxing magnificently on the Champs-Elysees?

Or would the focus be on the sheer passion of a huge, fervent crowd which lined the streets on Montmartre and around Sacre-Coeur?

That last element illustrated a sport in rude health and again raised the question of why organisers had not run the traditional closing stage over the scenic cobbled hill before its debut visit last year.

Pogacar, the rarely beaten 27-year-old Slovenian, is widely regarded now as cycling's greatest of all time.

The fifth Tour win helps in that respect, matching fellow greats Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain – but Pogacar can also point to his many successes elsewhere in cycling's other huge events, such as one-day monuments.

Brutal Belgian Merckx stood alone as the sport's greatest before now, thanks to a similar versatility on the bike – capable, like Pogacar, of winning in all formats: time trials, cobbles, high mountains and even some sprints.

But perhaps what elevates Pogacar to the top now is his respectful demeanour, paying tribute as he did in Paris to every one of his domestiques by name, before thanking his family.

He also shepherded his young UAE-Team Emirates-XRG team-mate Isaac del Toro across the line on more than one occasion during this year's race when his own job was done.

The fact Pogacar achieved what he did while most of his team-mates - and possibly even himself - suffered sickness across the second half of the Tour is even more remarkable.

The Tour de France still is, after all, one of the hardest events in elite sport.

The Tour de France has a chequered history that cannot be forgotten.

"He knows what the record is," Lance Armstrong said on social media following Sunday's result, referring to Pogacar.

The American's record of seven Tour de France victories between 1999 and 2005 has long since been wiped from the record books following the revelation of his systematic doping.

And those in the sport have fairly diligently avoided mentioning his name since.

But the night-time anti-doping tests during this year's Tour, which the International Testing Agency (ITA) told BBC Sport were undertaken as an "exceptional operation" and because time was of the essence, once again raised questions in a sport which doesn't need them, thanks to that dark past.

Testing at such anti-social hours is rare and requires additional permission, and some suspect it may have been a factor in Jonas Vingegaard's Tour-ending crash after he was woken at 2am the previous night, and Pogacar himself at 5am.

Others were tested at night, too, and all riders were tested during the race. But what were the ITA looking for?

They wouldn't say, specifically, but one possible explanation for night-time testing of professional cyclists appears to be to gather as much information as possible to try to understand micro-dosing. That is where an athlete could take performance-enhancing drugs, such as red blood cell stimulant EPO or anabolic steroids, in very small quantities to evade detection on the Athlete Biological Passport, which is endorsed by the World Anti-Doping Agency (Wada) and used across cycling.

There is no suggestion of wrongdoing in the case of Pogacar, Vingegaard or any of those tested at night this year.

Past findings produced by Wada suggest micro-dosing could evade detection methods, and so the scope to cheat in professional sport remains, meaning all efforts must be taken to ensure nobody beats the system.

The ITA cannot confirm when the results of the Tour tests will be made public, but EF Education-Easypost boss Jonathan Vaughters told BBC Sport: "Doubts? Actually [those tests] solve my doubts."

Vaughters, who doped during his riding career, is now reformed.

He said during this year's race: "If we had 24-hour testing in 2001 when EPO tests were first introduced we would have had a huge number of riders excluded from the sport, including me. And it would have saved 25 years of drama.

"So I mean we wouldn't have had to go through Lance Armstrong... The problem would have been solved immediately in 2000.

"If you introduce a low enough dose of a peptide hormone, the clearance time can be four hours - if you take it at 11 it'll be out of the system at 3am, so it makes a difference. The testing technology is evolving quickly.

"If you want to watch a clean sport, watch cycling, most other sports' testing is a complete joke.

"Why is cycling so hyper-focused? History. This is human F1 car racing; this is edge of human performance; boundaries are always going to be pushed."

Many riders and team bosses won't go near the 'D' word, and the consensus is 'believe what you are seeing' when Pogacar accelerates away and wins by, at times, a matter of minutes, and when others perform their own remarkable feats in the saddle.

Huge numbers of people do believe what they see.

About 500,000 spectators turned out in Paris on Sunday, with 180,000 around Montmartre alone.

And it doesn't stop at the Tour de France, as many of the bigger races on the calendar are seeing notably bigger numbers.

"You can't get to certain parts to watch it any more, everyone has been there all day. Especially this year," said one journalist at Paris-Roubaix in April.

"There's so much traffic and so many people."

And many fans have noticed the increase in numbers.

Another 500,000 people were estimated to have lined the roads up to Alpe d'Huez last Friday, as videos emerged on social media of crowds setting up camp days before, drinking and partying prior to the race arriving.

At the end of Friday's stage, Movistar's Colombian climber Einer Rubio was even involved in a harrowing incident when he crashed, face-first, into the back of one of the service cars belonging to Pogacar's team, breaking the glass.

The car had been forced to stop abruptly when a spectator fell immediately into its path.

Rubio was forced to abandon the race after being given 20 stitches in hospital.

The presence of Britain's women's Tour winner Lizzie Deignan and record Tour stage win holder Mark Cavendish on the Champs-Elysees on Sunday was a timely reminder that Britain will hosts six stages of the men's and women's Tour de France races next summer.

It will be summer when British fans hope Netcompany Ineos Cycling's new injection of investment will pay dividends – after they failed to win a stage in this year's race – and riders such as Tom Pidcock can light up the race on home soil.

Some 30.2m people cycled at least once in Britain in the past year, according to British Cycling, which is the highest number it has been since 2019-20.

While Pogacar will probably prevent it happening in 2027, many thousands of Britons are still expected to flock to witness the race in motion.

title: Pogacar wins fifth Tour title amid Paris finish drama
description: Slovenian Tadej Pogacar wins the Tour de France for a record-equalling fifth time.
fullText:
Slovenian Tadej Pogacar won the Tour de France for a record-equalling fifth time.

The 27-year-old UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider crossed the line on Paris' Champs-Elysees in the peloton, to join Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain as the endurance event's most successful male riders.

All-conquering Pogacar raised the idea that his remarkable reality is proving stranger than fiction, describing it as "something you wouldn't even maybe write in a story book".

The three-week Grand Tour's final stage was won by the Netherlands' Mathieu van der Poel of Alpecin-Premier Tech after a frantic charge to the line on the French capital's famous cobbles in which he pipped team-mate Jasper Philipsen of Belgium by inches.

Pogacar's victory means he is positioned by many as the greatest cyclist of all time, superseding the achievements and status of Belgian legend Merckx.

It also marks Pogacar's third Tour win in succession and includes a record-breaking ascent of the iconic Alpe d'Huez on stage 19, when he sealed another dominant victory.

It was the last of five stage wins in a race in which Pogacar used his explosive launch and unmatchable metronomic pace to see off his rivals, who for some time have had virtually no answer.

Pogacar has won almost every major race in the sport, including the Tour of Flanders, Giro d'Italia, Milan-San Remo, Road World Championships, Giro di Lombardia and Liege-Bastogne-Liege.

Pogacar was booed by some fans during the Tour, as his performances are often so far ahead of any of his peers that some feel frustrated the sport is losing its competitive edge.

He now has 127 wins in an eight-year elite professional career.

"Victory is really special," said Pogacar. "Thank you to all the fans and my team.

"But the biggest thanks goes to all my family who support me all my life. My parents - without them I would not be standing here five times already.

"Seven Tours and seven times on the podium, and five wins, is something you wouldn't even maybe write in a story book, and it's unbelievable for me.

"It's a magnificent podium with some incredible champions to fight with.

"It's a shame Jonas [Vingegaard] crashed out this time and many others. I hope they have a quick recovery and next year we fight again."

The famous final stage, which for the overall contenders is an unchallenged formality, typically becomes a flat bunch sprint.

Last year organisers ASO introduced a circuit which takes on a cobbled climb over the city's famous Montmartre hill, changing the parcours enough to encourage the heavier, more powerful riders to challenge for victory.

On Sunday it was powerhouse classics legend Van der Poel who took victory after charging away with 11km remaining with Pogacar.

Pogacar and Van der Poel led through the picturesque and narrow lanes over Montmartre and past Sacre-Coeur, where some fans had mobile phones knocked out of their hands as the riders squeezed past at speed, before Pogacar began to fade after three weeks of dominance and showing no weakness.

Van der Poel, whose strength and staying power allow him to pull out gaps in gruelling one-day races, just managed to stay ahead of a chasing pack which included several sprinters and was rapidly closing, before he crossed the line, collapsed off his bike and lay under a barrier, breathing heavily for several minutes.

Van der Poel added this prestigious victory on the famous cobbles to many of the sport's biggest one-day races, such as multiple victories in Paris-Roubaix and the Tour of Flanders.

He said: "We have a saying in Dutch that it has to come for your toes. I don't know where this came from, but not from my toes."

The stage was reduced from 133km to 89km after the redirection of emergency services to help tackle wildfires in south-west France.

The one rider who has broken Pogacar's stranglehold of cycling's biggest race in the past was Denmark's Vingegaard, who won in 2022 and 2023.

But this year the 29-year-old Visma-Lease a Bike rider abandoned after breaking his collarbone on a easy right-hand bend on stage 15.

The mistake was very unlike Vingegaard's near perfect technique and execution as a rider, and attention soon turned to scrutiny of the International Testing Agency (ITA), which had awoken Vingegaard at 2am to carry out an anti-doping test.

Other riders had the same treatment, including Pogacar at 5am, but the ITA said there was "exceptional circumstances" to take the night tests, which are rare and require additional permission.

It is not known when the test results will be published.

Pogacar's only other real rival was the much-improved Belgian Remco Evenepoel of Red Bull-Bora-Hansgohe, who finished six minutes 26 seconds behind overall.

Third place went to Pogacar's Mexican team-mate Isaac del Toro, who won stage two thanks largely to Pogacar's babysitting pace in the lead-up to the line.

It would not be the only time Pogacar would aid Del Toro, 22, sacrificing his own potential victory on Saturday's brutal 'queen' stage to Alpe d'Huez to consolidate Del Toro's place on the podium.

Del Toro's white jersey for the best young rider came at the expense of France's new 19-year-old star Paul Seixas of Decathlon-CMA CGM. Seixas looked stronger than Del Toro at times on the climbs but faded substantially on Saturday.

Many think Seixas will be a rival to Pogacar in the future.

In the year when Britain's four-time Tour winner Chris Froome retired, his former team - now known as Netcompany Ineos Cycling - failed to record a stage victory in 21 attempts.

Ex-Ineos rider Tom Pidcock of Pinarello-Q36.5 won on Alpe d'Huez four years ago and returned to this race having achieved much with a new team built entirely around him.

The 26-year-old did not manage to win a stage, but he and his team will be satisfied with Pidcock's consistent battling riding, which earned him ninth in the general classification to build on third place in last year's Vuelta a Espana.

Fellow Briton Adam Yates, 33, showed great tenacity after falling ill on stage 16 and spending two days riding at the back of the field before helping pace Pogacar up a climb for victory on stage 19.

One of the most entertaining riders in the race was Ecuador's Richard Carapaz of EF Education-Easypost. He toiled earlier in the race before coming into great form to claim the king of the mountains' polka dot jersey.

He won stage 18 and Saturday's stage 20 after topping the race's highest point first and after 5,450km of climbing.

The green points jersey was awarded to Denmark's Mads Pedersen of Lidl-Trek, after tenacious riding on climbs he is not typically strong on to hoover up mid-stage points, alongside winning stage four.

He beat a number of sprinters to the jersey, including Philipsen of Alpecin-Premier Tech. Philipsen won stage 17 and fellow Belgian Tim Merlier of Soudal-Quick Step won three bunch sprint stages.

title: Normandy's D-Day World War Two beaches become UNESCO heritage site
description: PARIS, July 26 (Reuters) - The Normandy D-Day beaches where Allied forces landed on June 6, 1944, to fight Adolf Hitler's Nazi troops and go on to liberate France have become a UNESCO protected world
fullText:
PARIS, July 26 (Reuters) - The Normandy D-Day beaches where Allied forces landed on June ‌6, 1944, to fight Adolf Hitler's ‌Nazi troops and go on to liberate France have become ​a UNESCO protected world heritage site, the United Nations body said on Sunday.

• In a statement on its website, UNESCO said that the ‌beaches formed an "exceptional ⁠cultural landscape shaped both by the events of 1944 and by their ⁠enduring remembrance", which therefore justified becoming a protected heritage site.

• The Normandy D-Day beaches are ​regularly the ​focus of commemorations ​featuring world leaders from ‌the United States, Britain, Canada and France.

• Soldiers participating in the Normandy landings came from the United States, Britain, Canada, Belgium, Norway, Poland, Luxembourg, Greece, Czechoslovakia, New Zealand and Australia. ‌Some 177 French commandos also ​took part.

• The assault ​marked a decisive ​stage in the liberation of Europe ‌from Nazi Germany in ​World War ​Two.

• In total, 156,115 Allied troops either landed by sea -- on to beaches codenamed ​Utah, Omaha, Gold, ‌Juno and Sword -- or were airdropped behind ​German coastal defences.

title: Pogacar poised to join Tour greats with fifth title in Paris finale
description: Tadej Pogacar is set to win a record-equalling fifth Tour de France after Ecuador's Richard Carapaz takes a dramatic stage 20 to Alpe d'Huez.
fullText:
Tadej Pogacar is set to secure a record-equalling fifth Tour de France after a dramatic stage 20 saw Ecuador's Richard Carapaz clinch victory on Alpe d'Huez as Sepp Kuss crashed twice while leading in the last few kilometres.

If Pogacar avoids a race-ending crash on Sunday's final stage to Paris, in which the overall standings are traditionally not contested, he will become the joint-most successful rider in the Tour's history alongside Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain.

Pogacar, 27, of UAE Team Emirates-XRG, finished the three-week Grand Tour's 'queen' stage in fourth place after helping his 22-year-old Mexican team-mate Isaac del Toro provisionally seal third place on the overall podium and the young rider classification's white jersey.

The pair crossed the line together with their arms around each other's shoulders after Pogacar paced a suffering Del Toro up the final climb.

Pogacar will claim his fifth overall yellow jersey in Paris by six minutes and 26 seconds over Belgium's Remco Evenepoel of Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe, after Evenepoel finished the stage in second, 26 seconds behind Carapaz, after a late charge.

"I did my best to help Isaac," said Pogacar afterwards. "Massive respect for what all the guys have been doing in the past three weeks. I finally experienced [being a domestique] myself and I already before appreciate [the] work of team-mates, but now it's like another level.

"It was goosebumps [as we crossed the line together]. [It] was fantastic and one for the memories."

On his future, he added: "I definitely will not be doing this for too much [of a] long time, I think. Isaac showed great potential, but we don't put any pressure yet on Isaac."

Race organisers ASO announced during the stage that Sunday's finale will have its distance reduced from 133km to 89km after the redirection of emergency services to help tackle devastating wildfires in the south-west of the country.

Traditionally, the final stage sees the sport's sprinters battle for the line on the famous Champs Elysees cobbles, but a new section over Montmartre allows riders with more sustained power the potential to steal a breakaway win.

The most demanding stage of the whole race was left to the penultimate day, in which riders had to climb 5,450 metres across three hors category climbs covering 170.9km to finish in the iconic Alpe d'Huez ski-resort for a second time in two days.

American Kuss of Visma-Lease a Bike was part a large early breakaway which contained riders looking for a stage win, and attacked alone with about 25km to go.

The 31-year-old looked to have found the strength which helped him win the Vuelta a Espana in 2023 and seemed set to hold on to a slender lead for victory.

But the often unflappable Kuss was on the ragged edge and crashed coming out of a tunnel approaching Alpe d'Huez town.

He maintained his lead, but soon after crashed again on a right-hand corner after getting his line wrong, his rear wheel sliding on dust at the edge of the road before coming to a stop, half off his bike and leaning into safety netting which prevented him from falling down a sheer drop.

The tenacious Carapaz, of EF Education-Easypost, swept past Kuss and into the lead - the 2019 Giro d'Italia winner, eventually taking his second stage win in three days and also securing victory in the king of the mountains competition.

"[I was] not really scared," Kuss told TNT Sports afterwards. "I was just annoyed because we drove down it this morning and I looked at that corner and thought: 'Ah that's a pretty descent corner, no problem in the race,' so I took it pretty full-on.

"It was a bit more of a corner than I expected. My wife won't let me race my bike anymore - she always tells me not take risks on the downhills, but you've got to have a little adrenaline rush every once in a while."

Typically, on a stage such as this one in the French Alps, Pogacar would be expected to deliver yet another masterclass but he held back to help Del Toro, who at one point was starting to struggle on the Col du Galibier, to defend his white jersey and third place overall from French sensation Paul Seixas of Decathlon CMA-CGM.

The 19-year-old Seixas finally ran out of energy on the final mountain of the race and is set to finish fourth in the general classification, 11 minutes and 56 seconds down on Pogacar's overall time.

Britain's Tom Pidcock of Pinarello-Q36.5 finished the stage 16th, nine minutes and three seconds down, and will finish ninth overall in the GC.

Denmark's Mads Pedersen of Lidl-Trek will win the green points jersey in Paris on Sunday just by finishing as he leads Belgium's Jasper Philipsen of Alpecin-Premier Tech by an uncatchable 82 points.

title: Lyles, Richardson ease into 100m semis at US athletics championships
description: Olympic gold medallist Noah Lyles and Sha'Carri Richardson eased into the 100m semi-finals at the US athletics championships on Thursday.Lyles, who captured 100m gold at the Paris Olympics in 2024, won his heat in 9.97sec to book his semi-final berth with the second-quickest time of the day behind the 9.96 posted by former world champion Christian Coleman.
fullText:
Olympic gold medallist Noah Lyles and Sha'Carri Richardson eased into the 100m semi-finals at the US athletics championships on Thursday.

Lyles, who captured 100m gold at the Paris Olympics in 2024, won his heat in 9.97sec to book his semi-final berth with the second-quickest time of the day behind the 9.96 posted by former world champion Christian Coleman.

Richardson, the 2023 world champion and 2024 Olympic silver medallist, topped the women's heats in 10.90sec.

Richardson will be a heavy favorite for the title on Friday, with Melissa Jefferson-Wooden -- a treble gold medallist at last year's world championships -- opting to race the 200m only this week.

Lyles called his championships opener a good warm-up "just to get the engine firing."

But he predicted a "fast final" on Friday on the Icahn Stadium track, where Usain Bolt set a 100m world record of 9.72sec in 2008 -- a mark the Jamaican eventually lowered to the current 9.58.

Coleman, the 2019 world champion and the 60m indoor world record-holder, was also pleased with his "really smooth" start to the meeting.

"I was able to break 10 (seconds) without really hitting the gas like I know I can, so I feel good about it," said Coleman, who topped the times despite racing into a slight headwind of 0.3m/sec.

Kenny Bednarek, a two-time Olympic silver medallist at 200m, won his 100m heat to advance.

Among a handful of finals on the opening day of competition, Woody Kincaid surged late to win the men's 10,000m in 30min 13.66sec ahead of 2024 Olympic bronze medallist Grant Fisher, who clocked 30:14.46.

Sydney Vaught won the women's 10,000m in 33:36.98.

Isaac Grimes claimed his second straight men's long jump title, clearing 8.18m on his final attempt. Malcolm Clemons was second with a leap of 8.07m.

title: Model recruiter who introduced young women to Jeffrey Epstein found dead in France
description: A French professional model recruiter who for over a decade arranged for the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to meet multiple models, was found dead in his home near Paris on Monday.
fullText:
A French professional model recruiter who for over a decade arranged for the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein to meet multiple models, was found dead in his home near Paris on Monday.

Daniel Siad's body was found in his house in Colombes, a suburb of the French capital, Marie-Céline Lawrysz, deputy public prosecutor at the Nanterre Judicial Court, told CNN in a Wednesday statement.

An autopsy will be performed on the body to determine the cause of death.

CNN'S Katie Polglase recently interviewed Siad, who said he had no reason to believe two women he had recommended to Epstein – and who had told CNN that Epstein had abused them – had been harmed by him.

Even after Epstein's 2008 conviction on sex crimes, modeling-industry insiders like Siad continued seeking business ventures with him, invited him to fashion events, and allowed him to associate with their companies.

Siad said Epstein had assured him he had paid for his crimes and that "this would never happen with anybody" that Siad referred to him.

"I trusted him and believed this guy was a professional person," he told CNN. "I never heard anything from anyone I introduced to him who came back to me that they had a bad situation. I believed this guy is a professional person."

Siad said he had believed Epstein was a casting director for Victoria's Secret and the modeling agency MC2. CNN found no evidence to support that claim.

Files released by the Department of Justice show Epstein paid tens of thousands of dollars to Siad.

In one message, Siad wrote: "Cute French girl in Marrakesh… She said that she will (be) happy to meet you."

Siad separately said that Epstein had asked him for help finding an assistant.

In a 2018 email, Siad wrote that he was looking for a "good looking young assistant" for Epstein.

After enjoying two impressive seasons under Hansi Flick, Ferran believes he has earned the opportunity to become a central figure in Barcelona’s long-term plans.

Instead, the club’s sporting direction has pointed elsewhere, with Julian Alvarez identified as the preferred option to lead the attack following Robert Lewandowski’s departure.

That development has significantly altered Ferran’s outlook, and Barcelona transfer news now suggests a move to PSG is the most likely outcome if both clubs can reach an agreement.

Ferran entered the summer expecting discussions over a new contract after establishing himself as one of Barcelona’s most consistent attacking performers.

Despite that progress, Barcelona never approached him with a renewal proposal.

Ferran Torres is facing an uncertain future at Barcelona. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images)

The lack of movement came as a surprise to the player, who had anticipated a clear sign of confidence after proving his value over the past two campaigns.

According to the report, that silence played a significant role in changing the forward’s perspective on his future at the club.

At the same time, PSG intensified conversations with the Spanish international, with negotiations now progressing positively.

Although personal discussions have advanced, any transfer will still require Barcelona and PSG to agree on a financial package.

Beyond the contract situation, Barcelona’s transfer strategy has provided another indication of where Ferran stands in the club’s hierarchy.

Journalist David Bernabeu explained that the forward never felt he was viewed as the natural successor to Lewandowski.

Discussing Ferran’s perspective, he said, “I suppose in his heart he thought: ‘And why not be the main bet for the number nine?'”

PSG move is gathering pace for Ferran Torres. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)
